summary: A short granite tower on a treeless island at the mouth of Machias Bay, Maine, built in 1822-23 and long counted among the foggiest stations on the coast.

access.note: Not open to the public; best seen from a boat.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends records a first tower of 1822 that collapsed in April 1823 and a rebuilt tower; New England Lighthouses dates the present tower to 1823. The NRHP nomination says the station was ordered built in 1822 and has never been rebuilt (and its data sheet gives 1819 for the tower, apparently a typing error). Not settled by a primary record.
NRHP nomination lists the fog signal building as built 1856; USLHS and LighthouseFriends give 1884, when the Daboll trumpet was installed in a new brick building.

notes_for_editor: Rich in secondary sources (LighthouseFriends, NRHP) but only partly checked against primary records. Not checked: the 1820s lighthouse correspondence behind the 1822/1823 collapse and rebuild; Isley and Humphrey are from LighthouseFriends only. Tower first-year conflict and fog-building year (1856 vs 1884) are unresolved; see resolved_conflicts. Princeport: NRHP calls it a ship rescued by the keepers; the 1893 Life-Saving report lists it as a British schooner served by the Cross Island Station crew. Ella G. Eels date (1906) is LighthouseFriends/USCG-historian snippet only; the 1905 LSS report lists an Ella G. Eells in November 1904 at City Point, Massachusetts, probably a different incident. Holbrook: the Kennebec Journal OCR gives a different spelling of Foss and a stated age of 43 that sits in a column that may belong to another item; the story uses LighthouseFriends/roster for his age (26) and cites the newspaper only for the drowning. The USLHS roster gives Isaac Stearns from 1842, LighthouseFriends says he took charge 24 February 1841. 1918 fog-hours figure (1,906) is OCR text in Bulletin p. 53 (22 per cent of a year would be about 1,927 hours), and the Bulletin does not say in the snippet which year it measures. LHB page numbers are scan pages (printed numbers unconfirmed); the 1892 item is in the volume binding fiscal 1891 and 1892. Bulletin page numbers are the PDF pages as printed by corpus. Annie S. date: paper of 3 Sept 1902 says Sunday night (31 Aug) per dateline 'September 8' OCR. Keepers matched by roster order, not table position. Verifier 2026-10-22: Foss is 'Justin A.' in the roster and Bulletins but the 1918 newspaper OCR prints 'Austin'; roster used. Bessie May: LighthouseFriends puts all three 1923 vessels in 1923 but the Bulletin entry is in the 1922 volume (19 September); story states the disagreement. NRHP buildings account (dwelling destroyed before 1949, rain shed to 1944) conflicts with LighthouseFriends (demolished 1974); story states both. NRHP calls the part it covers 'South Libby Island', LighthouseFriends 'Little Libby'; the 1895 Board report says 'southwest end of the southwesterly of the Libby Islands'; story follows the Board. Bulletin 1918 fog figure is fiscal year 1918 and 'highest on the Atlantic coast' (Point Reyes was higher nationally). Roster lines checked against roster.py output: all 118 match.
